prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study used a viral vector to deliver the Gsx1 gene into the spinal cord of animals with a contusion injury to test if it aids recovery.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Animals treated with Gsx1 showed better movement skills and sensitivity to touch compared to those that did not receive the treatment.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In the early stage after injury, the treatment caused cells lining the spinal cord to revert to a more primitive, stem-cell-like condition.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The treatment also steered a specific type of precursor cell away from dividing and toward forming nerve insulation and connections.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: In the long term, the treatment changed the mix of nerve cells in the spinal cord to favor a type that sends activating signals.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: There was a notable increase in nerve cells that use the chemical messenger glutamate to communicate.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Blocking a specific gene in the precursor cells reduced the beneficial effects of the treatment on both cell changes and movement recovery.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue
